one_line_description.value: Mermaid CLI (mmdc) is an open-source command-line tool that takes a Mermaid diagram definition file as input and generates an SVG, PNG, or PDF file as output.

access_notes.value: No API access to gate — it is an open-source npm package run locally; no credentials, plans, app review, or registration are required. Integration would require invoking the local mmdc binary or Node.js module directly.

community_mcp_servers.quote: A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that generates visual diagrams from Mermaid code using the Mermaid CLI tool.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Distributed via npm with version-tag releases (e.g., 11.15.0); no separate API versioning or deprecation/sunset policy documented.

verdict_reason: Mermaid CLI is an open-source local command-line tool (npm package) that renders Mermaid definitions to SVG/PNG/PDF; the official README describes no hosted or network API and no authentication. There is no public service endpoint to call, so a hosted/API integration cannot be built without wrapping the local binary or Node.js module. Composio's catalog also has no matching toolkit.
main_blocker: No hosted/public API — local CLI tool only.
open_questions: Name ambiguity: several search results (e.g., github.com/noahsabaj/mermaid-cli) are an unrelated AI coding-assistant CLI that shares the 'Mermaid' name; only github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli was treated as the target.

No authentication mechanism exists for Mermaid CLI itself; auth-themed search hits referenced a different product requiring provider API keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, etc.), not the mermaid-js CLI.
Release notes mention a Node.js `run()` API, but it is a local library interface, not a hosted API, and no API reference page was captured in SOURCES.

No vendor-operated MCP server was found for mermaid-js/mermaid-cli; only a community MCP wrapper (locupleto/mcp-mermaid-diagram). Mermaid Chart (separate SaaS, same origin team) reportedly hosts an MCP at mcp.mermaid.ai but this was not verifiable in the supplied sources.
Rate limits, webhooks, OAuth scopes, sandbox environment, and official SDKs are not documented; they are likely not applicable to a local CLI, but no explicit evidence was found.
